01 BOTTOM LINE

SOURCE OPINION GS Research forecasts STOXX 600 EPS to grow 18% in 2026 and 7% in 2027, far above euro area nominal GDP growth of 3.3% and 2.8%, because more than half of STOXX 600 revenues are generated outside Europe and sales-weighted GDP drives earnings. ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate⟩ C-fc23cff004ad51 C-1bee61b27b7d52 C-798eca834705be C-ef344246172350 C-d6212804b26b74

SOURCE OPINION The article argues global rather than domestic growth is increasingly relevant for European listed companies, implying investors should gauge European earnings against global/sales-weighted growth. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩ C-d6212804b26b74
MODEL INFERENCE If sales-weighted global growth and a weaker euro hold up, STOXX 600 earnings can stay resilient even with weak domestic euro area growth; the earnings strength depends on external demand rather than Europe's economy.

01 BOTTOM LINE

FORECAST GS expects earnings growth to at least halve across major regions in 2027 (US 36% to 11%), with IT slowing from ~90% to 45%, Communication Services from 34% to -5%, and Energy from 99% to around -10%, as AI capex growth peaks and oil prices moderate. ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate⟩ C-20c6472f838987 C-16a03de78d4649 C-ad7a302a455361 C-9f1fcac5dfedc9

MODEL INFERENCE The broad earnings deceleration — driven by peaking AI capex contribution (turning to a -5pp drag by 2028) and falling oil — is a headwind for capex beneficiaries (chips, Industrials) and commodity sectors, favouring companies that can sustain growth and stable margins.

our hypothesis TaskUs (TASK) — exposed — would be hurt IF this holds: “AI adoption spreads beyond technology into the broader economy.” (source opinion) [s03.0]: AI adoption automates the labor-intensive support and moderation tasks it sells, pressuring per-agent volumes as clients reduce human headcount. · basis (the model's): services — outsourced digital support and moderation · 10-K filed 2026-03-05 (0001829864-26-000012): the filing states no revenue-source sentence naming a way of earning in the words this check reads — not found is not wrong; read the filing
our hypothesis ASGN (ASGN — not verified by the SEC) — exposed — would be hurt IF this holds: “Firms reduce headcount as AI tools are adopted, lowering labor costs though causation not established.” (model inference) [s03.1]: If adopters cut headcount, demand for contract staffing placements falls, reducing its billable hours across nonmanufacturing clients. · basis (the model's): services — IT and professional staffing placements · not checked — no verified US listing — no annual report to read
our hypothesis ManpowerGroup (MAN) — exposed — would be hurt IF this holds: “Firms reduce headcount as AI tools are adopted, lowering labor costs though causation not established.” (model inference) [s03.1]: AI-driven headcount reductions shrink demand for temporary and permanent placements, its core fee base tied to client hiring. · basis (the model's): services — temporary and permanent staffing placements · 10-K filed 2026-02-23 (0001193125-26-064113): the filing states no revenue-source sentence naming a way of earning in the words this check reads — not found is not wrong; read the filing
our hypothesis ServiceNow (NOW) — exposed — would benefit IF this holds: “AI adoption spreads beyond technology into the broader economy.” (source opinion) [s03.0]: AI adoption spreading into broad-economy workflows drives demand for its agentic automation products that replace manual processes. · basis (the model's): subscription — workflow automation and AI software subscriptions · 10-K filed 2026-01-29 (0001373715-26-000007): its revenue-source sentence names subscription

01 BOTTOM LINE

SOURCE OPINION GS forecasts modest further tightening into early 2027 (Fed hikes Dec/Mar, ECB final hike Dec, BoE to 4.25%, BoC to 3.0%, BoJ to 2.0%) but expects central banks generally to end hiking earlier and cut sooner than markets price, implying scope for front-end rates to fall. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩ C-2bdc710d8ffff5 C-ed9615021e50be C-262e7c1dfef83a C-a6bfd881dbe58e C-fc92f5e25d8223 C-279ae4be501cda C-d8aa5bbbf0d82e C-709646520c3d36 C-ef5325261c3092 C-e69a13dee6d53e
⚠ UNRESOLVED REVIEW — The sentence lists BoC 'to 3.0%' and BoJ 'to 2.0%' and several specifics. Cited spans support ECB 2.25% 2027Q4, BoE 4.25% Feb, BoC two hikes to 3.0% in 2027H1, BoJ hikes to 2.0% terminal, and the dovish-vs-pricing opinion. But the Fed 'hikes Dec/Mar' claim is not in the cited spans (C-46005aa23c61f6 is only in the pool, not cited), and the broad 'expects central banks generally to end hiking earlier and cut sooner than markets price' goes beyond the cited opinion span which only speaks of 2027 dovish view.
SOURCE OPINION GS frames its dovish-vs-pricing view as a boost to both equities and bonds and as scope for front-end pricing to fall further through 2027. C-2bdc710d8ffff5
⚠ UNRESOLVED REVIEW — The cited opinion span supports a dovish-on-rates view but does not mention equities or bonds as beneficiaries. The equities/bonds framing is unsupported by this single cited span.
MODEL INFERENCE If GS is right that policy peaks lower than priced, front-end and forward rates fall, a tailwind for both bonds and equities; the thesis depends on inflation decelerating as GS expects.

01 BOTTOM LINE

FORECAST GS forecasts most EM central banks in CEEMEA and LatAm to cut through 2027, and Asian rates to stay flat or rise slightly but below market pricing except in Taiwan; it argues markets overestimate EM inflation risk because inflation was low pre-shock, EMs are cyclically weaker than DMs, and EM currencies have held up on healthy external balances. C-d6a94793fc242d C-3a3bf7a0183be4
⚠ UNRESOLVED REVIEW — The cited spans support 'most central banks to cut through 2027' and 'forecasts below market pricing except in Taiwan', but the specific regional breakdown (CEEMEA/LatAm cutting vs Asia flat/rising slightly) and the three-part inflation argument (low pre-shock inflation, EMs cyclically weaker, currencies held up on external balances) are not in the cited spans.
FORECAST The article's view implies scope for EM rates to fall more than priced, supporting EM bonds, though energy is the key upside inflation risk. C-d6a94793fc242d C-3a3bf7a0183be4
⚠ UNRESOLVED REVIEW — The cited forecast spans support rates falling more than priced, but the claims about 'supporting EM bonds' and 'energy is the key upside inflation risk' are not in the cited spans.
MODEL INFERENCE If GS is right, EM local-currency bonds could rerate higher as front-end rates fall below what markets price, with energy prices as the main upside risk.
